sections.title: DNA Zoo chromosome-length assemblies
sections.description: Hi-C maps with the genome assemblies they were used to scaffold, shared by the DNA Zoo Consortium. Large downloads: check your disk space first.

examples.title: Cheetah (Acinonyx jubatus)
examples.description: A chromosome-length cheetah assembly (aciJub1_HiC, 2n=38) with its Hi-C map. Shows scaffolding of a draft genome into chromosomes: contigs, scaffolds and the assembly file used to build them.

publications.title: De novo assembly of the Aedes aegypti genome using Hi-C yields chromosome-length scaffolds
publications.citation: Dudchenko O, Batra SS, Omer AD, et al. 2017. Science 356(6333):92-95.

Draft genome of the cheetah
publications.citation: Dobrynin P, et al. 2015. Genome Biology 16:277. Draft assembly GCA_001443585.1.

files.description: Hi-C contact map (needs conversion to HiCT format)

attribution.acknowledgement: DNA Zoo asks that its 3D de novo assembly methods paper is cited and that the acknowledgments of a paper using these data include: "Unpublished genome assemblies and sequencing data for the cheetah (Acinonyx jubatus) are used with permission from the DNA Zoo Consortium (dnazoo.org)."
attribution.restrictions: The provider states no formal licence. Where a draft genome used by DNA Zoo was made by others and is unpublished, respect any restrictions set by its creators.

examples.title: Yellow fever mosquito (Aedes aegypti)
examples.description: The AaegL5.0 yellow fever mosquito assembly (2n=6) and its Hi-C map, the genome that demonstrated chromosome-length scaffolding with Hi-C. Three large chromosomes make the structure easy to read.
